f.title: FDA deletes patient and research-subject identifiers before public release
f.statement: The names or other information which would identify patients or research subjects in any medical or similar report, test, study, or other research project must be deleted before the record is made available for public disclosure.
f.clause: 21 CFR 20.63 Personnel, medical, and similar files, paragraph (a)
f.applicability: Records held by FDA; medical or similar reports, tests, studies and research projects, and adverse event reports on human drugs, biologics and medical devices. The text draws no distinction between domestic and foreign cases.

f.title: Delete patient and research-subject identifiers from records before submitting them to FDA

f.applicability: Records held by FDA; medical or similar reports, tests, studies and research projects, and adverse event reports on human drugs, biologics and medical devices. The text draws no distinction between domestic and foreign cases.
f.exceptions: FDA may later request the names separately.

f.exceptions: Deletion may be justified under another exemption, e.g. § 20.61.

f.title: Requests for all records about an individual are denied without the individual's written consent
f.statement: A request for all records relating to a specific individual will be denied as a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy unless accompanied by the written consent of the individual named.
f.clause: 21 CFR 20.63 Personnel, medical, and similar files, paragraph (e)
f.applicability: Records held by FDA; medical or similar reports, tests, studies and research projects, and adverse event reports on human drugs, biologics and medical devices. The text draws no distinction between domestic and foreign cases.
f.exceptions: Unless accompanied by the written consent of the individual named.

f.title: Do not disclose the identity of voluntary reporters or persons in adverse event reports in response to a request, demand or order
f.statement: The names and any information that would identify the voluntary reporter or any other person associated with an adverse event involving a human drug, biologic, or medical device product must not be disclosed by FDA or by a manufacturer in possession of such reports in response to a request, demand, or order.
f.clause: 21 CFR 20.63 Personnel, medical, and similar files, paragraph (f)
f.applicability: Records held by FDA; medical or similar reports, tests, studies and research projects, and adverse event reports on human drugs, biologics and medical devices. The text draws no distinction between domestic and foreign cases.
f.exceptions: Exceptions in paragraph (f)(1): written consent of both reporter and person identified, court order in medical malpractice litigation involving both parties, and release to the subject of the report. Identities of reporters required by Federal statute or regulation to report are governed by those laws.
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Safety governance; Reporting policy

f.clause: 21 CFR 20.63 Personnel, medical, and similar files, paragraph (f) (mandatory reporters)
f.applicability: Records held by FDA; medical or similar reports, tests, studies and research projects, and adverse event reports on human drugs, biologics and medical devices. The text draws no distinction between domestic and foreign cases. Curator note (not in the text): mandatory reporters include manufacturers, applicants and device user facilities.

f.title: Identities may be disclosed with written consent of both reporter and person identified; no duty to seek consent

f.title: State and local laws may not permit or require disclosure of reporter or patient identities
f.statement: No State or local governing entity may establish or continue in effect any law, rule, regulation, or other requirement that permits or requires disclosure of the identities of the voluntary reporter or other person identified in an adverse event report except as provided in § 20.63.
